decisions.question: How much does the amendment say about the library key: only that it differs between JIT and AOT (S33's finding), or what the key depends on?

options.label: JIT against AOT only
options.consequence: matches S33 and topic-codegen@v1's caveat, but leaves a reader believing two JIT processes agree; the Flutter tester and `dart run`, which topic-codegen@v1's catalog both uses, do not

options.label: what the key depends on, as measured
options.consequence: the row says JIT against AOT, and a Private names paragraph adds the measured dependencies: the library's URL and how many libraries load before it, so the runner, the import set and the import order all move it; longer text, every clause backed by the experiment

decisions.chosen: what the key depends on, as measured
decisions.why: Ten minutes of code settled it: the same library's key is @22518013 under `dart run` and `dart test`, @21518013 under the Flutter tester, @18518013 under AOT, @28518013 when six libraries are imported ahead of it and @22518013 when the same six come after it; another URL changes the last six digits. Stating only JIT against AOT would have been true and misleading, since catalog runs under either JIT runner.

decisions.question: Does the private-name row need a behavior case, and if so what does it assert?

options.label: no case
options.consequence: G9 keeps its two cases, which test public names only; a FunctionRef.of that strips the key violates G9's rule and the new row yet passes every case (S6 shows it does today)

options.label: a case pinning the JIT key
options.consequence: asserts e.g. `_privateTwice@NNNNNNNN`; the value moves with the conformance library's imports, the test runner and the SDK, so the case would fail on changes that break nothing

options.label: a case asserting the @ and a key, never the value
options.consequence: asserts the name matches `^_privateTwice@.+$` and `^_reduceQuietly@.+$`, equals itself within the process, and is unequal to `FunctionRef.named('_privateTwice')`; stable across programs and runners; fails only if the producer strips or drops the key, or if a future SDK stops rendering the key, which would also make the row wrong

decisions.chosen: a case asserting the @ and a key, never the value
decisions.why: It closes a real coverage gap in G9 (a stripping or anonymizing FunctionRef.of now fails this case and nothing else, S5) without pinning a process-dependent number. Its one dependency on the VM's rendering is of the same kind as the existing G9 case asserting 'buildCheckoutUi', so it adds no new class of SDK sensitivity. A signal that would have changed my mind: a consumer binding this suite under a runner that is not the VM.

decisions.question: Where does the new text go: one table row, or a row plus a paragraph?

options.label: row only
options.consequence: short, but a table cell cannot carry the key's dependencies or the consequence for G7 equality across programs

options.label: row plus a Private names paragraph
options.consequence: the row shows what each private form renders per compiler; the paragraph states what the key depends on, the consequence for definitions, graphs and graph documents, the cross-references, and that it adds no guarantee

decisions.chosen: row plus a Private names paragraph
decisions.why: The step asked for the row and the consequence; the consequence is a sentence, not a cell. The row covers every private form the probe measured (top-level, static, instance method, named constructor of a public class, constructor of a private class) so no reader has to extrapolate, and the obfuscated and web cells come from the same probe.

decisions.question: G9's gloss reads 'which on the VM is the name of a top-level function, a static method without its class, or a method tear-off', inexact for a private name; and the paragraph after the table says the catalog runs 'where names are as written'. Edit either?

options.label: leave G9 and the sentence verbatim
options.consequence: smallest diff; the new case still traces to G9's rule, but two sentences of the contract stay inexact for private names, which is what this consistency pass exists to fix

options.label: add a clause to G9's gloss and say 'public names'
options.consequence: G9 gains 'with `@` and its library's key after a private name'; the sentence after the table says 'where public names are as written'; the rule itself, its number and every other clause stay

decisions.chosen: add a clause to G9's gloss and say 'public names'
decisions.why: Both sentences describe what the rule yields; the rule already yields the key, so the edits narrow nothing and oblige the producer to nothing new. Leaving them would make the new case look as if it tested something G9 does not say. The step framed the change as a statement of existing behavior, and the Versioning line records it as such.

decisions.question: Does the contract say what the key looks like, so a tool can compare up to it, as topic-codegen@v1 allows?

options.label: say nothing about its form
options.consequence: topic-codegen@v1's 'compares up to that key' stays undefined for a tool author

options.label: state its form as observed
options.consequence: 'The key is `@` followed by digits; outside an obfuscated build, removing each key gives the name as written', with a measured example; a descriptive line under the table's 'on the pinned SDK', not a guarantee, and the case does not assert digits

decisions.why: It gives 'up to that key' a concrete meaning at the one place that describes rendering, and it is measured for every private form in the probe, including the constructor of a private class where the key sits mid-name. If the VM ever changed the form, only this descriptive line would be wrong, and the case would still hold as long as the key follows an @.

decisions.question: Which cross-references does the Private names paragraph cite?

options.label: topic-codegen@v1 only
options.consequence: points the reader at the caveat for the catalog, but not at the worked avoidance

options.label: topic-codegen@v1 and nidana.integration D8
options.consequence: names the caveat (the catalog's document against an AOT `bus.toGraph()`) and the design that avoids it (public transformers), so a reader sees both the consequence and the remedy

decisions.why: Both help a reader: one states the consequence for a consumer's artifact, the other is the tree's own example of avoiding it. topic-codegen@v1 is cited, not edited, as the step requires.

decisions.question: Could the amendment break a consumer, which would need a v2 and so a stop?

options.label: compatible, keep v1
options.consequence: a Versioning line records the amendment; status stable and phase_ids final stay

options.label: breaking, stop for v2
options.consequence: a v2 with a migration note, which this run treats as a stop

decisions.why: No declaration, rule, canonical order, rendering rule, JSON key or schema changes (S1: the schema diff is empty, the fixture diff is two private functions and one case). G9's rule already yields the key, so the producer's obligation is unchanged; the stand-in that follows the rule passes all 43 cases (S4). Checked consumers: the only binding of this suite is the producer's own (nidana_dart_contracts_test.dart); other contracts' fixtures reference FunctionRef only in navigation-api@v1's G13 case, which compares FunctionRef.of(_principalOf) within one process; no graph document fixture in any contract holds a private name. Checked phase scopes in `consumers`: nidana.runtime.1, .8, .11 compare definitions within one process (activation idempotency); nidana.navigation.3, .6 compare within one process; nidana.flutter.5 to .7 read `bus.toGraph()` in-process; nidana.tooling.codegen.1, .5 to .11 check catalog documents only for public fixture transformers (its note on function references); nidana.integration.2 to .8 use public transformers (D8). experiments.question: What does FunctionRef.of's rule yield for each private form under each runner and compiler, what does the VM's library key depend on, and does one G9 case cover the private-name row without pinning a key?
experiments.finding: The VM renders `@` and the library key after each private identifier (`_hidden@K`, `_format@K`, `Holder._internal@K`, `_Holder@K.`, `_Holder@K._secret@K`); AOT with --obfuscate keeps `@K` after an obfuscated name; dart2js -O1, -O4 and dart2wasm give anonymous. For one library, K is @22518013 under `dart run`, its rerun, another entry file with the same imports, and `dart test`; @21518013 under the Flutter tester; @18518013 under AOT; @28518013 (JIT) and @24518013 (AOT) when six libraries are imported ahead of it; @22518013 when the same six come after it; a copy at another URL in the same process gets @23284448. So K follows the library's URL and how many libraries load before it. Suite: the stand-in of model-reconcile-amends, copied unchanged, passes all 43 cases; structure holds (G9 3 fixtures; nine contracts, 0 problems); the conformance library analyzes clean; a FunctionRef.of that strips the key, or makes a private name anonymous, fails the new case alone; before the amendment the stripping defect passed every case.
